verdict=$(sed -n 's/^Verdict:[[:space:]]*//p' "$record" | head -1)
if [ "$verdict" != "no-blocking-dependencies" ]; then
  echo "the change record's verdict is '$verdict'; the only verdict that finishes this stage is 'no-blocking-dependencies'."

  exit 1
fi

findings.message: Design D7 and handoff H1 claim that setting `fetch-depth: 0` on the checkout of the `check` job lets the published build see the history ('deploy.yml calls this workflow, so the published build sees the history too'). But `.github/workflows/ci.yml:40-43` runs `git fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin main` in 'Check data-only paths' before `pnpm build`. As far as I know, a `--depth=1` fetch into a full clone marks the fetched commit shallow, and on a push to main that commit is HEAD, so `git log` in resolveAppRevision again sees one commit. A data-only HEAD then gets the `unreadable-<instant>` value and shows a notice, so the app-delivery scenario 'The published build sees the history' and M2 fail in production. The H1 patch and README must also handle that step (e.g. fetch without --depth, or run the revision resolution against the unshallowed history), and D7 must say so.

Task 1.2's verification cannot pass as written: it expects `grep -rniE "version number|build number|auto-update" packages/client/src docs/glossary ...` to show these words 'only under *Never:*', but existing `docs/glossary/settings.md:11` (Deploy time) says 'a stand-in for a version number. ... *Not:* a version number.', which is not under *Never:*. No task updates the Deploy time entry, although the new App revision takes over its 'stand-in for a version number' role and lists 'version number' as a *Never:* word. Add a task (or extend 1.1/1.2) to change the Deploy time entry, or fix the verification.

Task 6.1 and design D6 plan `scripts/cityData/readDumpDate.ts` as new, but `packages/client/scripts/cityData/download.ts:86` already defines a function `readDumpDate` (it reads the dump date from the archive entry time), and `scripts/cityData/checkCityData.ts:46` already checks `source.dumpDate` of the committed file. The plan adds a second function with the same name for a related concept in the same module and splits dump-date validation from its existing check, without naming or adding a glossary owner for the 'date of the city data'. glossary.md says: 'Do not write a new function, type or constant for the same concept anywhere else' and 'A change that introduces a new domain concept adds its glossary entry in the same change'. Rename or merge it with the existing owner, and give the concept a glossary entry.
